1976.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1976-77 ed. Vol. II, Table 106 (State Individual Income Taxes: Rates, July 1, 1976), Table 107 (personal exemptions, July 1, 1976) and Table 108 (standard deduction, July 1, 1976). Table 106 prints a joint schedule (2.75%-7.75% on $1,500 steps to $7,500) and, in the special-rates column, a separate single schedule: 2.25% on the first $750 rising by 1% per $750 step to 7.25% on $3,751-$4,500 and 7.75% over $4,500. Table 107 fn: personal exemptions same as federal ($750 in 1976); Table 108 fn: standard deduction same as federal. Starts from federal taxable income. Deduction = $750 personal exemption per person; the standard deduction (Utah follows the federal definition, income-dependent with a low-income allowance) is left out as in this file's later years. Federal income tax deductible (not modelled).

1977.notes: Bridged: no ACIR edition describes 1977. The 1976-77 ed. (Table 106, July 1, 1976) and the 1979-80 ed. (Table 82, July 1, 1980) print the same single (2.25%-7.25% on $750 steps to $4,500, 7.75% over) and joint (2.75%-7.75% on $1,500 steps) schedules, and the Tax Commission's History of the Utah Tax Structure (the source cited; individual income tax legislative history) lists no rate change between HB 74 (1976, effective for 1976) and HB 168 (1981); its rate table (income.xlsx, 'Individual Income Brackets', 1975-1981 column) gives the same rates. SB 32 (1979) let heads of household use the joint schedule from 1980. Starts from federal taxable income with Utah exemptions/deductions frozen at 1974 federal law: deduction = $750 personal exemption per person (Tax Commission income.xlsx 'IIT Exemption and Deductions', $750 for 1973-1986); the standard deduction (15% of AGI, min $1,300, max $2,000, income-dependent) is left out as in this file's other years. Federal income tax deductible (not modelled).
